node.title: Re^2: Multiple Packages in a Module?
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
If foo.pm contains Package Foo::Bar (for test purposes) but there is also an available Foo/Bar.pm, my understanding is that the file will be retrieved to satisfy the package-reference. Hence, the double-declaration within the test-case foo.pm file will not be effective because the contents of this file will not be read unless a use Foo; declaration coincidentally preceded it

I'm sorry, but this just plain doesn't make sense. package Foo::Bar doesn't cause anything to be loaded, and a use Foo; statement doesn't affect the loading of Foo::Bar in any way.

... an unacceptably-dicey proposition which makes your test-case dependent-for-success upon the exact layout of the source-code being tested, while also being fairly-blind to the possibility of the interpreter doing something that you didn’t expect.

IMO you are casting too much doubt on what is in fact a deterministic process (see the other replies in this thread for details).

If you are advising caution, then I would recommend against PERL5LIB, since there are quite a few other things that can affect [doc://@INC] and the loading of modules. (In case one wants to be paranoid, [doc://require] can be given an absolute filename to load, or one can use [doc://do] with absolute pathnames directly. But that should be very rare, since the correct approach is fixing @INC in the first place.)

But all of this is currently a thought experiment anyway, since it only applies if the OP makes the mistake of saying use Foo; or use Foo::Bar; in addition to loading test_v1 via use or require. And [LanX] has already given the [id://1217380|advice] regarding [doc://%INC], which [id://1217497|can be used] to prevent those files from being loaded in the first place.

Update: Typo fix, thanks [LanX].
